findings.claim: The screen synchronization routine enumerates NSScreen.screens, attempts a UInt32 NSScreenNumber from deviceDescription, updates an existing dictionary entry or creates a panel for each usable identifier, then orders out/removes entries for identifiers no longer seen.
unknowns: The separate active-expansion/fullscreen presentation policy has not been completely reconstructed.

findings.claim: The transparent outer panel envelope is 820*s wide and min(900*s,max(120,screen.frame.height-80)) high, centered horizontally and aligned at screen.frame.maxY. This is not the collapsed visible-notch size.

With screen safeAreaInsets.top > 1, both auxiliary top areas and a right.minX-left.maxX gap > 80 yield width ceil(gap)+1+20 and height ceil(top)+1. A usable top inset without a usable gap yields width240 and height ceil(top)+1. Missing screen or top<=1 yields60x8.
findings.rounding_authority: Swift FloatingPointRoundingRule.up enum identity and corroborating ARM64 FRINTP branches; decompiler integer-cast renderings are not the rounding authority.

findings.claim: The scale helper returns1.0 when safeAreaInsets.top>1. Otherwise it performs the code path NSUserDefaults.standardUserDefaults.boolForKey(ClickyStreamMode), returning1.5 for true and1.0 for false.
unknowns: No installed user preference was read; its actual current value remains unknown.

findings.claim: A separate presentation-size helper supplies unscaled visible content widthW and heightH. The visible frame is (screen.midX-W*s/2,screen.maxY-H*s-delta,W*s,H*s). delta=4*s for encoded presentation case1 on a screen with top<=1; otherwise0.
unknowns: Encoded presentation case numbers have not been exhaustively mapped to original Swift enum/source names.
The large presentation-size routine has an unrecovered jump table and truncated high-p-code; its many branch sizes do not establish the complete visible state machine.
SwiftUI clipping/shape/animation and exact runtime transitions remain unverified.

findings.claim: Creation allocates the NotchPanel subclass using style mask0x80 (borderless0 plus nonactivating128), backing2(buffered), deferfalse; then sets opaque=false, clear background, shadow=false, movable=false, movableByWindowBackground=false, hidesOnDeactivate=false and excludedFromWindowsMenu=true.
unknowns: Creation contains a conditional orderFrontRegardless path; runtime visibility was not observed.

findings.claim: Creation registers the panel with the overlay coordinator using its boolean flag1. That flag selects integer26 in0x101301454;0x1013065e0 sends setLevel: only if the current level differs.
unknowns: This proves the creation/registration path, not every later level or system-window interaction transition.

findings.claim: Collection behavior combines canJoinAllSpaces1, ignoresCycle64, fullScreenAuxiliary256, and either transient8 or stationary16 according to keepsNotchVisibleThroughMissionControl. The constructor initially clears that field.
canBecomeMainWindow helper returns0. canBecomeKeyWindow returns the inverse of the byte isTemporarilyRefusingKeyStatus at object offset8; the panel initializer clears that byte.
unknowns: The Objective-C thunks contain unreliable recovered Swift/ObjC ABI casts; these conclusions use helper instructions and the decoded ivar identity.

findings.claim: The two metadata-backed entries rejected as missing procedures in the unseeded partial Program became analyzable through documented REA_GHIDRA_SEED_FILE; no private provider mutation or new product feature was required.
unknowns: Seeds are caller assertions backed by metadata/direct-call observations; they are not original source method names or discoveries of auto-analysis.
Other unseeded unreachable functions still report no-procedure; future focused seed profiles can include those explicit entries.
